limitations: Approval covers only the afternoon structure: expanded_afternoon (first-day Rosh ha-Shanah Minchah) and expanded_tashlikh, read as XML. It is not an overall source, export or batch acceptance, and no source scans were read in this review.

Musaf was NOT reviewed. This group has no Musaf XML or order entry. The only Musaf material is musaf-intro-tail-runtime-check.json, a technical proof marked UNACCEPTED, and you said proofs alone don't count as review. I could not locate the generated Musaf file: I have no directory-listing tool, and integration-projects-v2/project/index.xml does not exist. So the priest/cantor/congregation calls, the dream prayer and שלום substitution, the full three verses from this edition when there are no priests, the single final blessing, and Hayom are all unreviewed, and this approval says nothing about Musaf.

Afternoon items checked in the XML and found correct: (1) Order is Ashrei, Uva letziyyon, then the quorum-only first half Kaddish (with its preface), then Va'ani tefillati, Torah reading, silent Amidah, repeated Amidah, Avinu Malkenu, full Kaddish, Aleinu, mourner's Kaddish. (2) Va'ani depends only on Shabbat, not on a minyan. (3) The Torah reading needs Shabbat plus a minyan and has three aliyot (Kohen, Levi, Yisrael), each with Barekhu, the blessing before, the Ha'azinu reading and the blessing after. Ha'azinu is right for Rosh ha-Shanah day 1 on Shabbat, and only day 1 can fall on Shabbat. (4) There are two half Kaddishes when both Shabbat and a minyan apply. (5) The silent Amidah is declared silent and not a repetition, and contains the full third blessing. (6) The repetition needs a minyan and has the reader role. It leaves out Adonai sefatai, Elohai netzor and Yehi ratzon, has Qedushah after Gevurot, then the range from Uvekhen ten pachdekha to Qadosh attah, and no priestly blessing at Minchah. (7) Modim derabbanan carries the congregation role. (8) Avinu Malkenu is weekdays only. (9) Full Kaddish and mourner's Kaddish need a minyan; Aleinu does not. (10) Every condition/endConditional and declare/endDeclare pair is correctly matched and scoped.

Tashlikh items checked and found correct: it requires Minchah and either day 1 not on Shabbat, or day 2 on a Sunday (which happens when day 1 was Shabbat). It has an 'after Minchah' rubric. The Shabbat-day-1, weekday-day-2 and non-Minchah cases are all excluded.

URNs: every transclusion uses a canonical urn:x-opensiddur:text: URN. Shared units (Uva letziyyon, Torah Barekhu, Qedushah, Modim derabbanan, Avinu Malkenu, the Musaf-conclusion Kaddish and Aleinu, half Kaddish) are reused rather than duplicated. The mourner's Kaddish adds a project identifier (@hasiddur_hashalem-birnbaum-1949-he), which is allowed for references.

Unverified, outside this group: the shared prayer:amidah/qedushah/ledor_vador unit must end at 'ki el melekh gadol veqadosh attah', with no weekday closing 'ha-el ha-qadosh' or a closing chosen by condition. Otherwise the repetition would carry the wrong or a doubled closing before Uvekhen. The runtime check only proves the Uvekhen-to-Qadosh-attah range holds the Rosh ha-Shanah closing.

Unverified: the hodaah range from veal_kullam to vekhol_hachayyim should include Ukhtov and the hodaah closing. Whether it does depends on milestone scope in the shared silent-Amidah unit, which is not in this group and has no runtime check. Shabbat insertions inside the reused Shacharit units were also not visible here.
Qedushah call-and-response roles (congregation, then reader) are not marked in this structural XML. They may be inside the canonical Qedushah units, but I did not verify that.

The Torah service is only codex-written English rubrics for taking out and returning the scroll. No Hebrew rubric and no hagbahah or ark-procession texts are encoded; whether the source prints them was not checked. The reader (חזן) and congregation (קהל) role labels are in Hebrew only.

Bilingual and page turning: no step in the encoded sequence makes the reader turn to another page; everything is pulled in by transclusion. However, the page-boundary audit (a technical proof, marked UNACCEPTED) lists Hebrew pages 312–326 but English pages only 313–319, so how Hebrew-only pages 320–326 line up with English was not confirmed from the source. The mourner's Kaddish is Hebrew only, borrowed from the Birnbaum siddur because this volume doesn't print it, and has no English, as the coverage note says.

The appendix327+ limit is accepted as an honest incomplete-volume boundary, not a claim that those prayers are encoded. The runtime proofs (runtime-precheck, page-boundary-precheck, actual-range-call-check) were treated only as backing for the XML reading.
